question: Which Quezon watercourse names does the official 7 August 2026 flood advisory provide, and can they be safely reconciled with existing CALABARZON leads?
purpose: Preserve a useful official watercourse-name inventory while preventing duplicate or invented river identities and separating historical hazard context from fish or current safety data.

sourceDetails.title: General Flood Advisory No. 14
sourceDetails.sourceTextLabel: Watercourses likely to be affected; “Quezon: Rivers and its tributaries particularly …”
sourceDetails.reviewLimit: The notice is a dated weather/flood advisory; this review does not treat it as current hazard advice.

possibleDuplicatesOrCompoundLabels: Upper Umiray is linked to the Umiray River lead at name/locality level; its “Upper” reach and route remain unverified.
Lugan Malaybalay is linked to DPWH Annex D-2 row 98 at Region IV-A principal-basin name level only; channel identity, exact LGU allocation, and boundary remain unresolved.
Lower Bolbok (Lawaya) may combine a reach and alternate name.
Pagsanjan matches an existing name but may refer to a different watercourse than the current lead.
Agos is crosswalked to the existing individual Agos River lead at name/locality level; its exact advisory reach and relation to the separate JICA system lead remain unresolved.
Bucal (Lalangan), Lugan Malaybalay, and Upper Kilbay – Catabangan are retained verbatim as compound labels pending parsing.
Lower Bolbok (Lawaya) is crosswalked to the principal-basin name only; the lower reach route remains unresolved.
Malaking-Ilog is crosswalked at basin-name level; its exact relationship to the Malaquing Ilog channel remains unverified.
Iyam is crosswalked to the official Iyam River name within its WQMA system, but the advisory does not identify a reach.
Macalelon crosswalks to separate source-named river and principal-basin leads at drainage-system level; the advisory reach and exact channel-to-basin topology remain unverified.
Catanauan is crosswalked to the official river name and locality, but no specific flood-advisory reach is established.
Silongin Lagda remains a compound advisory label: the EMB-listed Silongin River is not linked until an official source explains “Lagda”.
Yabahaan in the advisory matches the spelling variant Yabahan River in DENR DAO 2025-28 and EMB reporting at San Andres locality level; the exact advisory reach remains unresolved.

Bigol, Guinhalinan, Calauag, Pandanan, Sta. Lucia, Maapon and Tignoan have direct BMB-DENR river-name/Quezon matches and same-named DPWH basin entries; the basin-to-channel relationship and exact advisory reach remain unverified.

Vinas crosswalks to the existing Viñas River lead by official source-name and Quezon locality context; its exact advisory reach is unverified and any relation to the separate Hinabaan lead remains unresolved.
reconciliation.reason: The advisory supplies 23 official watercourse labels. Eighteen have source-name/locality or basin-name crosswalks, including Agos at broad Quezon locality level, Anibawan in the BMB-DENR Atlas, Upper Umiray linked to the existing Umiray River lead at name/locality level, and Lugan Malaybalay linked to DPWH Annex D-2 row 98 at principal-basin name/region level only. Exact advisory reaches, routes, and basin extent remain unverified. Five labels lack a full source-name/locality crosswalk: Silongin Lagda is a partial match and four labels remain unresolved. This queue is not a count of unique physical rivers.

nextActions: Crosswalk the 5 labels without a full source-name/locality match against official DENR/Geoportal/LGU hydrography or a second source; resolve Silongin Lagda and exact reaches/routes independently.
Resolve exact advisory reaches and routes for crosswalked names separately, including the “Upper Umiray” qualifier and Agos system relationship.
Keep reach qualifiers and compound names separate in the evidence log until their feature relationship is established.
Never reuse this dated notice as current hazard, access, water quality, or fishing-safety advice.
Seek fish-specific studies separately; the advisory is not fish evidence.
nonClaims: The 23 entries are source-named candidates, not 23 verified unique waterbody entities.
No river route, geometry, fish presence/absence, salinity, legal status, access, or current flood risk is inferred.
The advisory-label crosswalk does not determine the exact Iyam or Catanauan reach or channel geometry.
The Macalelon river and principal-basin leads are separate and have no validated route or boundary geometry.
The Agos River lead remains separate from the Kaliwa-Kanan-Agos system lead; their exact relationship and the advisory reach are unresolved.
The Upper Umiray name/locality crosswalk does not verify the exact reach or channel route.
The Lugan Malaybalay crosswalk is to a principal river basin name/region row only; it does not establish a channel, exact LGU allocation, basin boundary, or connection to Malaybalay City, Bukidnon.
